 SCCH - 25 3 MVC 4044/2020  JUDGMENT The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 05.03.2020. 
2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 05.03.2020 at about 12.30pm when the petitioner was riding the Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-01-HJ-2024 on Varthur-Sarjapura Main Road, infront of Govt. Urdu School, Varthur, a Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-C-0032 came with high speed,
driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed the petitioner's Scooter and also dashed against the parked 407 vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AF-2312. Due to the terrible impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries. 
3. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Suraksha Hospital, provided first aid treatment and thereafter he was admitted and treated as an B. Anand vs Mohammed Ghouse on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121496291/
2 inpatient from 05.03.2020 to 19.03.2020, underwent surgeries and discharged with advice. So far he has spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards surgery and medical expenses, nourishment and transportation expenses. 
4. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, prior to the date of accident he was Electrical Contractor by profession and earning Rs.25,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he cannot attend his work permanently, resulting in loss of earning and he is put to great financial hardship and untold misery. The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Canter bearing No.KA-03-C-0032 and filed charge sheet against the driver in Cr.No.48/2020 punishable u/Sec.279, 337 of IPC. The 1st Respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of the Canter bearing No.KA-03-C-0032 and the 3 rd respondent being the Owner and 4th respondent being the insurer of the 407 Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AF-2312 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, this petition. 
5. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondent Nos.2 to 4 appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements. In spite of due service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this court hence, placed ex-parte. 
6. The objections of the Respondent No.2:
This respondent admits the issuance of the policy in favour of the 1st respondent in respect of the Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-C-0032. The driver of the Canter did not have a valid and effective DL at the time of accident. The Canter was used without having valid Permit and Fitness Certificate. There is non compliance of Sec.134(c)
and 158(6) of MV Act. It has denied the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and the manner of accident. The accident occurred only due to the negligent riding by the petitioner and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the Canter Lorry. Further it has denied the petitioner's age, occupation, income and other details of the Petitioner and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant. Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition. 
7. The objections of the Respondent No.3: 
The respondent No.3 has denied all those allegations and averments contained in the claim. He was never at fault with regard to the accident which the petitioner met. The vehicle was duly parked and the petitioner collided/dashed with the parked vehicle. 
The accident occurred solely on the negligence of the petitioner himself. As such, he prayed for dismissal of the petition against him. 
8. The objections of the Respondent No.4: 
This respondent denies all the averments made in the claim petition except admitting the issuance of the policy in respect of the TATA SFC-407 bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AF- B. Anand vs Mohammed Ghouse on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121496291/
3 2312. The driver of the insured vehicle did not have a valid DL as on the date of accident. The offending vehicle did not have a valid Permit to ply the vehicle as on the date of accident. There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act so this respondent is not liable to indemnify the 3rd respondent against the alleged cause of action. The petitioner himself dashed to the TATA SFC-407 bearing No.KA-02-AF-2312 and caused the accident. The Respondent insurer has further denied the manner of accident, petitioner's age, occupation, income and other details of the Petitioner and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant. Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition. 
9. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent acts of Driver of Canter vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-03-C-0032 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation? If so, what is the quantum? 
From whom payable? 
3. What order or award? 
10. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 14 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.17. Dr.Nagaraj B.N got examined as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.18 &
19. Petitioner has also got examined Smt.Renuka - Medical Record Department Official at Suraksha Multispeciality Hospital, Bangalore as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.20 & 21. On the other side, the Respondent No.2 has got examined Miss Ruchitha Renukesh - Senior Executive as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 & 2. The Respondent No.4 got examined Mr.Lakshmikant - FDA, RTO, Bangalore as RW.2 and got marked Exs.R.3 to R.5. The Respondent No.4 got examined Mr.Shreyas Bhat - Manager, Legal Claims as RW.3 and got marked Exs.R.6 to R.8.
11. Heard the arguments of the learned counsels for both the parties. 
The Counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the following decisions:
(i) 2015 AIR SCW 3169 : Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd., and Ors.
(ii) 2018 ACJ 1768 : Amrit Paul Singh and Anr. Vs. TATA AIG Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., and Ors.
(iii) MFA No.3323/2016 (MV-I) : Narasimha Raju Vs. Mansoor Ali Khan and Anr.
(iv) MFA No.1419/2013 (MV): H.P.Nagegowda Vs. N.Subramanya Kalluraya and Anr.
B. Anand vs Mohammed Ghouse on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121496291/
4 12. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
Issue No.1: Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:-
REASONS 13. Issue No.1: 
In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-C-0032 the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 7 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 7. PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination. The Respondent Nos.2 to 4 have denied the manner of accident and also denied the involvement of the respective vehicles in the accident. Further contended that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner himself. In the cross-examination of PW.1, he has stated that the accident spot was a junction with Three Roads. He has stated that the 407 vehicle was parked half on the road and half on the footpath. He has stated that road was a straight road. His two wheeler touched the right middle portion of the parked tempo. He has stated that the accident could have been avoided if the canter did not hit him. 
14. The FIR at Ex.P.1 was registered on 05.03.2020 at about 12.30pm on the same day of the accident on the complaint of petitioner at Ex.P.2. Ex . P.3 is the Wound Certificate shows the accident occurred on 05.03.2020 at about 12.30pm and in an RTA the petitioner sustained grievous injuries. 
Ex.P.4 is the spot mahazar shows the details and spot of the accident conducted on 05.03.2020 at 18.30. Ex.P.5 MVA report shows that petitioner's vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-HJ-2024 damaged to its front wheel mudguard, front body shape, rear wheel mudguard and tail lamp set, rear number plate and extra safety grill, rear both indicators, both sides body and foot board damaged. In the same manner the Canter vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-03-C- 0032 damaged to its front left side wheel fender, front left side corner, front left side indicator, front bumper on left side portion, front left side door and front left side extra cargo steps damaged and also 407 vehicle bearing No.KA- 02-AF-2312 damaged to its right side body slightly. Ex.P.6 sketch shows the spot of the accident. 
Ex.P.7 is the charge sheet filed against the driver of the Canter bearing No.KA- 03-C-0032 and the driver of the 407 Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AF-2312 after thorough investigation. 
15. The respondent No.2 has contended that the petitioner himself was negligent and there was also negligence on the part of the 407 Tempo. In order to prove the same, the respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Authorization letter and the copy of insurance policy as per Exs.R.1 & 2. During the cross examination of RW.1, he has admitted that the charge sheet is filed against Two vehicles. The accident took place in the broad day light at 12.30pm. The respondent No.4 has contended that the 407 vehicle was parked properly, the accident was caused due to the negligence of the petitioner and Canter driver. In support of the same, the respondent No.4 got B. Anand vs Mohammed Ghouse on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121496291/ 
5 examined its official as RW.3 and got marked authorization letter, copy of policy with terms and conditions and DL extract of the driver of Tempo as per Exs.R.6 to 8. During the cross-examination of RW.3, he has admitted that the charge sheet is filed against the Canter as well as Tempo drivers. 
Further admitted that as per police document the insured Tempo was on the left side of the Road. 
From the documents on record it is clear that the root cause of the accident was the Canter Lorry hitting the Two wheeler and the petitioner suffered injuries only because the 407 was parked on the road. If the 407 was not parked, the petitioner would get enough space to control his bike and he could have avoided injuries. Therefore, on overall perusal of the documents, this Tribunal holds that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Canter Lorry bearing No.KA-03-C-0032 and the negligent parking by the 407 vehicle in the ratio of 50:50. 
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held partly in the affirmative. 
16. Issue No.2:- 
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the Wound Certificate as per Ex.P.3. As per Ex.P.3 the petitioner has suffered Fibula Fracture and medial malleolus fracture, deep abrasions on medial side of right foot with loss of skin which are grievous in nature. 
17. The Petitioner got examined Smt.Renuka - Medical Record Department Officer at Suraksha Multipspecialty Hospital as PW.3 and got marked Consultation bill cum receipt and inpatient case sheet and X-ray films as per Exs.P.20 & 21. During the cross examination of PW.3, nothing worthwhile is elicited. 
18. The Petitioner also got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW.2 and got marked clinical report and recent X-ray as per Exs.P.18 & 19. He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and has stated about the physical disability of the right lower limbs at 41% and to the whole body at 14%. 
19. In his cross examination, PW.2 stated that, he has not treated the petitioner. Fractures are united as per the latest X-ray. The petitioner walks without any support and there is no shortening of the right leg. There is no fracture to Tibia but only to fibula and implants are in place. The petitioner can do Supervisory Work and he may face a little difficulty. 
20. The petitioner has averred that, at the time of accident he was an Electrical Contractor by profession and earning Rs.40,000/- per month. From the evidence of PW.2 it can be seen that the disability being suffered by the petitioner will impact his work. Therefore, this court deems it fit to consider the whole body disability at 10%. 
Monthly income:
21. The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was an Electrical Contractor by profession and earning Rs.40,000/- per month. In this regard he has produced notarized copy of Class-I Electrical Contractor License as per Ex.P.9 and Income Tax returns for the Assessment year 2013-14 B. Anand vs Mohammed Ghouse on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121496291/
6 to 2019-20 as per Ex.P.10. True copy of Work order (12 pages) as per Ex.P.15, True copy of Bank account statement issued by Bank of Baroda as per Ex.P.16 and Bank account statement issued by SBI as per Ex.P.17. 
The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the following decision:
MFA No.1419/2013 (MV): H.P.Nagegowda Vs. N.Subramanya Kalluraya and Anr. 
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that the Tribunal can rely on the Income Tax Returns as proof of Income. 
The It returns at Ex.P.10 shows that the Gross Income of the petitioner has increased from Rs.3,52,413/- in the year 2013-14 to Rs.5,39,168/- in the year 2019-20. 
Therefore, it can be inferred that Rs.45,000/- was his average monthly income. 
22. At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 48 years as could be made out from Ex.P.8/Notarized copy of DL. He was hale and healthy before the accident. Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:- 
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Suraksha Hospital, Bangalore as an inpatient from 05.03.2020 to 19.03.2020, discharged with advice to take follow up treatment. In this regard, he has produced Discharge Card at Ex.P.11 of Suraksha Hospital. Considering that the nature of injuries he has undergone is grievous and the duration of treatment , the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.80,000/- under this head. 
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES: 
The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc., In this regard, he has produced 118 medical bills as per Ex.P.13 for a sum of Rs.85,849/-. There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondent No.2. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head. 
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries. The petitioner has taken treatment for 15 days at Suraksha Hospital which can be made out from Ex.P.11 Discharge summary. Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least Two months time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him. Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.90,000/- under this head. 
B. Anand vs Mohammed Ghouse on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121496291/
7 iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:- 
On perusal of Ex.P.8/Notarized copy of DL, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01.08.1971 and the date of accident is 05.03.2020. Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 48 years. As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 13. However, Ex.P.15 is the work order from the year 2014 till 2020. The Bank Statement at Ex.P.16 relating to Bank of Baroda is not very clear about the amount credited. However, the Bank Statement of SBI at Ex.P.17 shows that the petitioner has received from MRKR Construction Rs.1,73,666/- on 22.05.2019, Rs.1,24,600/- on 05.07.2019,
Rs.1,24,600/- on 07.09.2019, Rs.1,94,374/- on 01.11.2019, Rs.47,704/- on 13.01.2020, Rs.36,382/- on 13.02.2020, Rs.51,636/- on 05.03.2020, Rs.85,966/- on 01.09.2020, RS.7,325/- on 05.09.2020, Rs.17,865/- on 20.11.2020, Rs.9,528/- on 17.03.2021, Rs.7,324/- on 18.03.2021, and from MEDA Construction Rs/52,734/- on 12.06.2020, Rs.21,678/- on 12.08.2020, Rs.6,503/- on 21.08.2020, Rs.16,777/- on 15.09.2020, RS.41,282/- on 11.11.2020, Rs.43,450/- on 30.12.2020, Rs.38,925/- on 16.02.2021, Rs.81,244/- on 18.03.2021, Rs.59,095/- on 26.04.2021, Rs.16,732/- on 10.06.2021, Rs.51,042/- on 15.06.2021, Rs.1,32,634/- on 27.06.2021, Rs.64,296/- on 25.08.2021, Rs.1,57,920/- on 14.10.2021, Rs.59,408/- on 01.12.2021, Rs.91,838/- on 24.12.2021, Rs.1,34,420/- on 25.01.2022, Rs.1,82,236/- on 24.02.2022 and Rs.13,000/-
on 21.04.2021, Rs.8,000/- on 22.06.2021 for Electrics. The date of accident is on 05.03.2020. The Bank statement at Ex.P.16 shows that the petitioner has continued to receive substantial amount of money from construction companies even two years after the accident. This clearly shows that, the petitioner has not suffered any loss of income. Therefore, he is not entitled to any compensation under this head. 
 (v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:- 
The Petitioner was aged about 48 years at the time of accident. He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 10% functional disability. The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life. Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts. Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head. 
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES: 
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospital, admitted for 15 days as an inpatient and discharged with advise. However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses. Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head. 
B. Anand vs Mohammed Ghouse on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121496291/
8 (vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES: 
As per the version of PW.2, the Petitioner has to undergo another surgery for removal of implants and the estimation of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-. In this regard neither the petitioner nor PW.2 has produced any estimation bill about further surgery. As per the evidence of Pws.1 & 2 and looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded to the Petitioner under this head. Therefore,
the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head. 
23. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.80,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.85,849/-
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.90,000/- period 4. Loss of future income NIL 5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/- happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/- nourishment charges 7. Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/-
TOTAL Rs.3,15,849/-
If it is rounded off it comes to around Rs.3,16,000/-
and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner. 
LIABILITY 24. And the respondent No.4 has also got examined FDA, RTO, Bangalore as RW.2 and got marked authorization letter, Interstate permit endorsement issued by State Transport Authority and copy of permit as per Exs.R.3 to 5. During the cross-examination of RW.2, has admitted that the 407 Tempo vehicle registered in their RTO and issued permit within state. 
The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the following decisions:
2018 ACJ 1768 : Amrit Paul Singh and Anr. Vs. TATA AIG Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., and Ors.
B. Anand vs Mohammed Ghouse on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121496291/ 
9 Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court India has held that in case of absence of valid permit, the insurance company can be directed to pay and recover. MFA No.3323/2016 (MV-I) : Narasimha Raju Vs. Mansoor Ali Khan and Anr. 
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has followed the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Amrit Paul Singh case and held that in case of absence of valid permit, the insurance company can be directed to pay and recover. 
However, in this case RW.1 has stated that interstate permit may have been issued from State Transport Authority. The respondent No.4 made all efforts to secure the document from State Transport Authority but in vain. Therefore, since the respondents did not prove their defence, this court cannot assumes that there was permit. 
The Counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the following decision:
2015 AIR SCW 3169 : Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd., and Ors.
Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that 'the claimants are entitled to claim entire compensation from both or any one of the joint tortfeasors.
25. Therefore, the respondents being the RC owners and the Insurer of both Canter Lorry and 404 Tempo vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner in the ratio of 50:50. However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent Nos.2 & 4/insurer has to indemnify the respondent Nos.1 & 3/insured and to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner. The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.3,16,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization. 
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed. Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the affirmative. 
26. Issue No.3: 
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER The petition is allowed with cost. 
 The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.3,16,000/- (Rupees Three  Lakhs Sixteen Thousand only) from the Respondents along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount. The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the B. Anand vs Mohammed Ghouse on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121496291/
10 said compensation to the petitioner.
 However, the Respondent Nos.2 &
 4/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest in the ratio of 50:50 before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award. 
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules. 
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-. Draw decree accordingly. (Typed to my dictation directly on the computer by the Stenographer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 9th Day of October 2024). 
(PRAKRITI KALYANPUR) XXIII ASCJ, MEMBER MACT, Bangalore.

2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 05.03.2020 at about 12.30pm when the petitioner was riding the Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-01-HJ-2024 on Varthur-Sarjapura Main Road, infront of Govt. Urdu School, Varthur, a Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-C-0032 came with high speed,
driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed the petitioner's Scooter and also dashed against the parked 407 vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AF-2312.
Due to the terrible impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

So far he has spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards surgery and medical expenses, nourishment and transportation expenses.
4. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, prior to the date of accident he was Electrical Contractor by profession and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he cannot attend his work permanently, resulting in loss of earning and he is put to great financial hardship and untold misery.

The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Canter bearing No.KA-03-C-0032 and filed charge sheet against the driver in Cr.No.48/2020 punishable u/Sec.279, 337 of IPC.

The 1st Respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of the Canter bearing No.KA-03-C-0032 and the 3 rd respondent being the Owner and 4th respondent being the insurer of the 407 Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-02-AF-2312 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.
5. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondent Nos.2 to 4 appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.
In spite of due service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this court hence, placed ex-parte.

6. The objections of the Respondent No.2:
This respondent admits the issuance of the policy in favour of the 1st respondent in respect of the Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-C-0032.
The driver of the Canter did not have a valid and effective DL at the time of accident.

There is non compliance of Sec.134(c)
and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and the manner of accident.
The accident occurred only due to the negligent riding by the petitioner and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the Canter Lorry.
Further it has denied the petitioner's age, occupation, income and other details of the Petitioner and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.
7. The objections of the Respondent No.3:
The respondent No.3 has denied all those allegations and averments contained in the claim.
He was never at fault with regard to the accident which the petitioner met.
The vehicle was duly parked and the petitioner collided/dashed with the parked vehicle.
The accident occurred solely on the negligence of the petitioner himself.
As such, he prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.

3 2312.

The offending vehicle did not have a valid Permit to ply the vehicle as on the date of accident.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act so this respondent is not liable to indemnify the 3rd respondent against the alleged cause of action.
The petitioner himself dashed to the TATA SFC-407 bearing No.KA-02-AF-2312 and caused the accident.

Issue No.1:

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-C-0032 the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 7 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 7.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination.

14. The FIR at Ex.P.1 was registered on 05.03.2020 at about 12.30pm on the same day of the accident on the complaint of petitioner at Ex.P.2.

15. The respondent No.2 has contended that the petitioner himself was negligent and there was also negligence on the part of the 407 Tempo.
In order to prove the same, the respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Authorization letter and the copy of insurance policy as per Exs.R.1 & 2.

If the 407 was not parked, the petitioner would get enough space to control his bike and he could have avoided injuries.

Therefore, on overall perusal of the documents, this Tribunal holds that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Canter Lorry bearing No.KA-03-C-0032 and the negligent parking by the 407 vehicle in the ratio of 50:50.
